items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: I remember Mongo used to make mention of sacred rhythms. ... Mongo Santamaria.

ctx.x: Wow. If you had a niece or nephew that was headed towards a career in jazz, would you have any real-life advice that you might tell them?

Yeah. Practice. Study and practice. Digest. And also, I would teach them the polymetric time. Because most of the people in the colleges are playing with the wrong time conception, man. They’re playing the notes they hear Charlie Parker play, but they’re playing with a time conception that comes from European music, which is monorhythmic. It’s not polymetric time. And so a big part of it is learning the right time conception. And the piano starts playing — Charlie Parker said he felt like the saxophone was…
